title: Word Ladder
keyIdea: Words are nodes, one-letter changes are edges: the shortest ladder is a BFS shortest path. Find neighbours by trying all 26 letters at each position and keeping words still in the set; erase (or mark visited) when queued so no word is queued twice.

approaches.name: BFS by levels with a visited set
approaches.idea: Return 0 if endWord is missing. Process the queue level by level; res counts levels; visited stops repeats.
approaches.why: Each word is queued once; each pop tries L·26 changes, each hashed in O(L).

approaches.name: BFS with (word, steps), erasing from the set
approaches.idea: Queue (word, steps); a word found in the set is erased and queued with steps + 1; return steps when endWord is popped.
approaches.why: Same work, and the word set doubles as the visited set.

options: All steps cost 1, and BFS reaches words in order of steps, so the first time it reaches endWord is the shortest ladder
